title: The completed-coefficient Koszul unit is a chain map
statement: Let T be a scheme, A a commutative ring, and d an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For r generators a_j and m>=0, extend the constant Koszul complex on a_j^(m+1) [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] along the residue-normalized scalar map to the completed coefficient sheaf A_T. Its degree-zero unit is the sheafification of 1 tensor 1. For any cochain complex C of A_T-modules, tensor these units with C using the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The resulting maps into B(C)=product_m(C tensor Q_m) are compatible with the Koszul transitions, so their composite with one minus shift is zero. The componentwise map c -> (u_C(c),0) into the prescribed shifted mapping cone is a chain map, with exactly the shifted-cone signs of completedAdicKoszulFibre. No boundedness hypothesis on C is required.

source.place: Prescribed completion unit and proof step 1: its degree-zero Koszul inclusions, compatible tensor units and explicit mapping-fiber differential.

proof.text: The compatible residue scalar map is the sheafification-adjunction transpose of the cone of finite scalar maps; uniqueness follows from sheafification and the limit projections. Form the sheafified section 1 tensor 1 in Koszul degree zero. Restrictions preserve both units. Transfer it through the normalized scalar-extension object equality and apply the unit-module/sections equivalence to obtain the unique degree-zero unit morphism.

Use the stated constant Koszul reindexing and transition construction from [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-koszul-completion]. The degree-zero Koszul differential to degree one is zero because the complex is extended from nonnegative chain degrees. The total-tensor summand differential formula and naturality of the right unitor show that tensoring a closed degree-zero unit defines a chain map.

The exterior transition fixes the zeroth exterior power. Apply constant-module functoriality and naturality of normalized scalar pure tensors to prove compatibility of the completed degree-zero units. Tensor functoriality gives compatibility of the tensor units. Each product projection of their composite with one minus shift is therefore zero, so the composite itself is zero.

Compute the differential of the shifted mapping-cone left inclusion using homotopyCofiber.inlX_d and the shift sign (-1)^(-1)=-1. The extra term is the component of the just-proved zero composite. The remaining term is the tensor unit chain-map identity, proving the displayed component equation for every pair of related degrees.

theorem completedAdicKoszulUnitF_comm (T : Scheme.{t}) (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A)
    (r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → A) (C : CochainComplex (CompletedAdicModules T d) ℤ)
    (p q : ℤ) (_hpq : (ComplexShape.up ℤ).Rel p q) :
    ((completedAdicKoszulProductUnit T d r a C).f p ≫
      HomologicalComplex.homotopyCofiber.inlX (-completedAdicKoszulOneSubShift T d r a C)
        p (p + (-1)) (by change p + (-1) + 1 = p; omega)) ≫
        (completedAdicKoszulFibre T d r a C).d p q =
      C.d p q ≫ (completedAdicKoszulProductUnit T d r a C).f q ≫
        HomologicalComplex.homotopyCofiber.inlX (-completedAdicKoszulOneSubShift T d r a C)
          q (q + (-1)) (by change q + (-1) + 1 = q; omega)
